overall: Washington DC reached a running maximum of 102.2°F at approximately 15:34 ET, and temperatures have been declining for roughly 3.7 hours at a velocity of -1.5°F/hr as of 19:15 ET. The day has been extremely hot, consistent with the active Heat Advisory, and the peak is almost certainly already in the books. Conditions are cooling off as expected for a July evening, with the NWS overnight low forecast at 81°F.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models showed some spread on the high end — GFS at 104.7°F was notably warmer than HRRR (102.1°F) and NBM (101.1°F) — but the INTRADAY model, anchored to the observed 102.2°F running max, now overwhelmingly (94.4%) favors the 102–103°F bucket. The NWS narrative forecast of 103°F was close but slightly above what was actually observed. With all four NWP models predicting peak timing at 16:00h and the actual peak occurring at 15:34 ET, timing was well-forecast and the post-peak decline confirms no further warming is expected today.
max_temp_prediction: With the observed running max locked in at 102.2°F, temperatures declining sharply at -1.5°F/hr nearly 4 hours past peak, and no convective or dynamic mechanism to reheat the atmosphere this late in the evening, today's TMAX is effectively determined at 102.2°F. The active even-bucket market's top bucket of 100–101°F (24.3% per D1_NOW) significantly underestimates the outcome — the intraday model's 94.4% weight on 102–103°F is far more credible at this stage. Confidence is very high that the final TMAX will be reported in the 102–103°F even bucket.
